answer: Nonce-Anchored Reply Chains. Each identity must answer a fresh challenge whose correct reply derives from the prior reply it gave, forming a chain only a persistent agent can extend; the anchor is the chained prior output, so replays fail. A falcon trace logs each step, and any fork invalidates the pearl of verified history, forcing sybils to rebuild full compute per identity. An attacker pays one full sequential computation per fake identity, making mass registration cost linear in real work.
